summary: Allocates a texture/render slot by index in an allocation pool. Validates the active count against the capacity and the requested index against the capacity, computes the 128-byte-aligned slot from the base pointer at this+0x34, and rejects already-in-use slots. Two allocation modes are selected by the sign of the flags byte at this+0x20: a free-list mode that links the slot onto the chain headed at this+0x38 (prev/next links at slot+120 and slot+124), and a compact-array mode that copies row data into a backing buffer and registers the slot in the index array at this+0x3C. Both modes mark the slot in use (bit 0x40) and increment the active count at this+0x30.

local_names.this: texture/render slot pool: flags 0x20, row count 0x24, capacity 0x2C, active count 0x30, slot base 0x34, free-list head 0x38, index array 0x3C, sub-context 0x50
local_names.v3: capacity value; also carries the slot flags byte and the returned count
local_names.v8: row count from this+0x24 used by the copy loop
local_names.v9: source dword pointer into the sub-context row region
local_names.v10: destination dword pointer into the copy buffer

operations.description: If the active count *(this+0x30) is not below the capacity *(this+0x2C), or the requested index a2 is not below the capacity, skip allocation entirely.

Compute the slot pointer v5 = *(this+0x34) + (a2 left-shifted by 7) (a 128-byte slot stride) and read the slot flags byte; if the in-use bit 0x40 is set the slot is already allocated and the function returns.
Branch on the signed flags byte at this+0x20: a value >= 0 selects the free-list allocation mode, otherwise the compact-array mode.

Free-list mode: read the free-list head at this+0x38 and walk its chain through the next links at +0x7C; append the new slot as the new tail (tail next link = v5), or make v5 the head when the list is empty. Then set the slot's prev link, zero its next link, and set the in-use bit 0x40.
Free-list mode: increment the active count at this+0x30.
Compact-array mode: TextureAllocationWithFormatSizeFlags(0) is invoked before the data copy step.

Compact-array mode: read the sub-context at this+0x50 and its copy buffer at +0x20 and its row region base at +0xC; for each row (row count at this+0x24) copy 4 dwords from the source row region (offset by 36 rows times a2 times the row count) into the copy buffer (offset by the active count times the row count left-shifted by 6), advancing 16 dwords per iteration.

Compact-array mode: store the current count as the slot id (v5[1]), register the slot pointer in the index array at this+0x3C at index = count, set the in-use bit 0x40, and increment the active count at this+0x30.
Return the caller's capacity/flag value v3 unchanged on the skipped paths, or the incremented count after a compact-array-mode allocation.
Invoked from the circular-buffer slot allocation path CircularBufferSlotAlloc (004CB540).

unresolved: Whether the flags byte at this+0x20 selects two genuinely different slot representations (free-list chain vs compact array) or two container modes of one pool is DERIVED from structure, not confirmed.

The purpose of the TextureAllocationWithFormatSizeFlags(0) call on the compact-array path (allocation with a zero format argument before the data copy) is unresolved; it may guarantee a backing buffer for the copy.
The exact meaning of the slot id dword at slot+4 is only partially resolved: it serves as the copy-stride row offset and as the value stored into the index array.

The linked-list tail-walk field bases in the packet (*(this+0x38) and *(*(*(this+0x38)+0x7C)+0x7C) at offset 0x7C) are canonicalized evidence for the next-link reads/writes at node+0x7C; the chain depth is not a confirmed constant.
